summary: The study describes the use of ozone (O3) as a post-treatment and coreactant with Mn(EtCp)2 in atomic layer deposition (ALD) to produce Mn5O8. The process involves sequential exposures of Mn(EtCp)2 and O3, leading to self-limited multilayer deposition of crystalline Mn5O8 with a high growth rate of 5.7 Å/cycle and a density of 4.7 g/cm³. The formation of Mn5O8 is attributed to the chemical equilibrium between Mn(II) and Mn(IV) oxidation states during the ALD process.
